readings.title: The Righteous Man of Uts
readings.subtitle: Job's piety and his family's feasts.
readings.text: [Job 1:1] There was a man in the land of Uts, whose name was Iyoḇ. And that man was perfect and straight, and one who feared <dn>Elohim</dn> and turned aside from evil. [2] And seven sons and three daughters were born to him. [3] And his possessions were seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys, and a very large body of servants, so that this man was the greatest of all the people of the East. [4] And his sons went and had a feast in the house of each on his day, and sent and invited their three sisters to eat and to drink with them. [5] And it came to be, when the days of feasting had gone round, that Iyoḇ would send and set them apart, and he would rise early in the morning and offer ascending offerings – the number of them all – for Iyoḇ said, “It might be that my sons have sinned and cursed <dn>Elohim</dn> in their hearts.” This Iyoḇ always did.

readings.title: The First Accusation
readings.subtitle: Satan challenges Job's integrity before YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Job 1:6] And the day came to be that the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to present themselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and Satan also came among them. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“From where do <dn>you</dn> come?”</dq> And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “From diligently searching in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“Have <dn>you</dn> considered <dn>My</dn> servant Iyoḇ, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and straight man, one who fears <dn>Elohim</dn> and turns aside from evil?”</dq> [9] And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “Is Iyoḇ fearing <dn>Elohim</dn> for naught? [10] “Have <dn>You</dn> not made a hedge around him, and around his household, and around all that he has on every side? <dn>You</dn> have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land. [11] But stretch out <dn>Your</dn> hand, please, and strike all that he has – if he would not curse <dn>You</dn> to <dn>Your</dn> face!” [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“See, all that he has is in <dn>your</dn> hand. Only do not lay a hand on himself.”</dq> And Satan went out from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The First Test
readings.subtitle: Job loses his possessions, his servants, and his children.
readings.text: [Job 1:13] And the day came to be when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the first-born. [14] And a messenger came to Iyoḇ and said, “The oxen were ploughing and the donkeys feeding alongside them, [15] when Sheḇa fell upon them and took them away, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the servants with the edge of the sword. And <dn>I</dn> alone have escaped to inform you!” [16] While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The fire of <dn>Elohim</dn> fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them. And <dn>I</dn> alone have escaped to inform you!” [17] While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The Kasdim formed three bands, and made a raid on the camels and took them away, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the servants with the edge of the sword. And <dn>I</dn> alone have escaped to inform you!” [18] While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “<dn>Your</dn> sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the first-born, [19] and see, a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. And <dn>I</dn> alone have escaped to inform you!” [20] Then Iyoḇ rose up and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and he fell to the ground and did obeisance. [21] And he said, “Naked <dn>I</dn> came from my mother’s womb, and naked <dn>I</dn> return there. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken away. Blessed be the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [22] In all this Iyoḇ did not sin nor ascribe wrong-doing unto <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Second Accusation
readings.subtitle: Satan afflicts Job's body, and his wife counsels him to curse Elohim.
readings.text: [Job 2:1] Again the day came to be that the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to present themselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and Satan also came among them to present himself before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“From where do <dn>you</dn> come?”</dq> And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “From diligently searching in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“Have <dn>you</dn> considered <dn>My</dn> servant Iyoḇ, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and straight man, one who fears <dn>Elohim</dn> and turns aside from evil? And still he holds fast to his integrity, although <dn>you</dn> incited <dn>Me</dn> against him, to destroy him without cause.”</dq> [4] And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “Skin for skin, and all that a man has he would give for his life! [5] “But stretch out <dn>Your</dn> hand, please, and strike his bone and his flesh – if he would not curse <dn>You</dn> to <dn>Your</dn> face!” [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“See, he is in <dn>your</dn> hand, only spare his life.”</dq> [7] And Satan went out from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and struck <dn>את</dn> Iyoḇ with loathsome sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. [8] And he took a potsherd with which to scrape himself while he sat in the midst of the ashes. [9] And his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Curse <dn>Elohim</dn> and die!” [10] But he said to her, “<dn>You</dn> speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Indeed, should we accept <dn>את</dn> good from <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and not accept <dn>את</dn> evil?” In all this Iyoḇ did not sin with his lips.

readings.title: The Arrival of the Friends
readings.subtitle: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar come to comfort Job.
readings.text: [Job 2:11] And three of the friends of Iyoḇ heard of all this evil that came on him, and each one came from his own place – Eliphaz the Těmanite, and Bildaḏ the Shuḥite, and Tsophar the Na‛amathite – and they met together to come to sympathise with him and to comfort him. [12] And they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and did not recognise him, and they lifted their voices and wept. And each one tore his robe and sprinkled dust on his head toward the heavens. [13] Then they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.

readings.title: Job Curses His Birth
readings.subtitle: He wishes for the day of his birth to be erased from time.
readings.text: [Job 3:1] After this Iyoḇ opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth. [2] And Iyoḇ spoke, and said, [3] “Let the day perish on which <dn>I</dn> was born, and the night it was said, ‘A male child has been conceived.’ [4] Let that day be darkness. Let not <dn>Eloah</dn> from above seek for it, nor let light shine upon it. [5] Let darkness and the shadow of death buy it back, let a cloud dwell on it, let all that blackens the day frighten it. [6] That night – let darkness seize it. Let it not be included among the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months. [7] Look, let that night be silent! Let no singing come into it! [8] Let those curse it who curse the day, who are ready to stir up Liviathan. [9] Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it wait for light, but have none. And let it not see the eyelashes of the dawn. [10] For it did not shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hide trouble from my eyes.

readings.title: Longing for the Grave
readings.subtitle: Job describes the peace and rest found in death.
readings.text: [Job 3:11] Why did <dn>I</dn> not die from the womb, come forth from the belly and expire? [12] Why were there knees to receive me? Or breasts for me to suck? [13] For now <dn>I</dn> would have been lying in peace. <dn>I</dn> would have slept – then <dn>I</dn> would have been at rest, [14] with sovereigns and counsellors of the earth, who built ruins for themselves, [15] or with rulers who had gold, who filled their houses with silver, [16] or as a hidden untimely birth, as infants who never saw light? [17] There the wrong cease raging, and there the weary are at rest, [18] the prisoners rest together, they do not hear the voice of the oppressor. [19] The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

readings.title: Why is Light Given to the Suffering?
readings.subtitle: Job questions the purpose of life amidst unbearable pain.
readings.text: [Job 3:20] Why does <dn>He</dn> give light to the sufferer, and life to the bitter of being, [21] who are waiting for death, but it does not come, and search for it more than treasures; [22] who rejoice exceedingly, they are glad when they find the burial-site? [23] Why does <dn>He</dn> give light to a man whose way has been hidden, and whom <dn>Eloah</dn> has hedged in? [24] For my sighing comes before <dn>I</dn> eat, and my groanings pour out like water. [25] For that which <dn>I</dn> greatly feared has come upon me, and that which <dn>I</dn> dreaded has overtaken me. [26] <dn>I</dn> have not been at ease, nor have <dn>I</dn> been undisturbed, nor been at rest, yet trouble comes!”

readings.title: Eliphaz's Rebuke
readings.subtitle: He questions Job's impatience and asserts that the innocent do not perish.
readings.text: [Job 4:1] And Eliphaz the Těmanite answered and said, [2] “If one tries a word with you, would you become impatient? But who is able to withhold himself from speaking? [3] See, you have instructed many, and you have made weak hands strong. [4] <dn>Your</dn> words have raised up him who was stumbling, and you have strengthened the weak knees. [5] But now it has come to you, and you are impatient; it strikes you, and you are troubled. [6] Is not your reverence your trust, the integrity of ways your expectancy? [7] Remember, please: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? And where have the straight ones ever been cut off? [8] According to what <dn>I</dn> have seen, those who plough wickedness and sow suffering reap the same. [9] Through the breath of <dn>Eloah</dn> they perish, and through the Spirit of <dn>His</dn> nostrils they are consumed. [10] The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, but the teeth of the young lions shall be broken. [11] An old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

readings.title: A Vision in the Night
readings.subtitle: Eliphaz recounts a spiritual encounter questioning mortal righteousness.
readings.text: [Job 4:12] And unto me a word was secretly brought, and my ear received a little of it. [13] Amid thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, [14] fear came upon me, and trembling, causing my bones to shake greatly. [15] Then a spirit passed before my face, the hair on my body stood up. [16] It stood still, but <dn>I</dn> could not discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes – silence, then a voice <dn>I</dn> heard, [17] Is mortal man more righteous than <dn>Eloah</dn>? Is man more clean than his Maker? [18] Look, <dn>He</dn> puts no trust in <dn>His</dn> servants, and <dn>He</dn> charges <dn>His</dn> messengers with straying. [19] How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed like a moth? [20] From morning till evening they are beaten down, they perish forever, with no one regarding. [21] Are not the cords of their tents pulled up? They die, without wisdom!’
